questions.questionText: What problem does hybrid search address?
options: It makes vector search run faster
Pure semantic search can under-weight exact keyword/identifier matches, so combining it with traditional keyword search catches both kinds of relevance
It removes the need for chunking
It only matters for very short documents
questions.correctAnswer: Pure semantic search can under-weight exact keyword/identifier matches, so combining it with traditional keyword search catches both kinds of relevance
questions.explanation: A query containing a specific error code or identifier might not be semantically distinctive, so combining keyword search with vector search catches cases embeddings alone might miss.

questions.questionText: How does re-ranking typically work in a two-stage retrieval pipeline?
options: It replaces vector search entirely with a single expensive pass over the whole collection
Retrieve a larger candidate set quickly with vector search, then apply a slower, more precise model to re-score just that shortlist
It randomly shuffles the retrieved results
It only re-ranks results after they've already been shown to the user
questions.correctAnswer: Retrieve a larger candidate set quickly with vector search, then apply a slower, more precise model to re-score just that shortlist
questions.explanation: Running the expensive, more accurate scoring model only on a small shortlist (rather than the whole collection) keeps the two-stage approach both fast and precise.

questions.questionText: What problem does Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) solve?
options: It speeds up the embedding computation
Top-k results by pure similarity can be redundant (near-duplicates); MMR balances relevance with diversity to cover more distinct information
It removes the need for a similarity threshold
It only applies to keyword search, not vector search
questions.correctAnswer: Top-k results by pure similarity can be redundant (near-duplicates); MMR balances relevance with diversity to cover more distinct information
questions.explanation: Without a diversity mechanism, the highest-similarity chunks can all restate the same fact; MMR penalizes redundancy with already-selected results to spread coverage across more of the actual information need.
